$comment: T7 (Agent 5): the REVIEWED BEHAVIOUR-CHANGE CATALOGUE for the permanent owner login (owner addendum 2026-11-04).
Every protection the restricted runtime logins (crewflow_app / crewflow_worker) gave that the owner login crewflow_owner cannot keep is one entry here,
with a severity, the test that proves the new behaviour, and its acceptance status: OWNER-ACCEPTED (the owner's final prompt section 2) or
NEEDS OWNER APPROVAL (not listed there). The final removal PR (#9) is gated on: every entry has a passing test, no entry is NEEDS OWNER APPROVAL,
and every existing test that asserted restricted-login behaviour is listed under migratedTests (migrated to this catalogue, or kept as a schema-role test).
A test is never flipped to 'passes' because the owner can now do the thing: the new behaviour is asserted AND recorded as a finding.

differences.change: The runtime login reads every tenant's rows of the 16 NOT FORCE pre-auth tables without injection (a missing tenant filter suffices).
differences.mitigation: M-T1 (FORCE + owner-only definer policy) protects normal code paths only

differences.change: Injected SQL has full DDL: NO FORCE / DISABLE RLS, ALTER POLICY USING (true), DROP TABLE, DROP SCHEMA core CASCADE.
differences.mitigation: semantic posture hash at boot and on a timer (M0 §6.4 #4)

differences.acceptance: OWNER-ACCEPTED (§2: persistence through roles or definers; credential-exposure impact)
differences.change: Backdoor LOGIN roles, re-granting the schema owner, replacing SECURITY DEFINER bodies, resetting crewflow_app's password survive rotation of the owner password.
differences.mitigation: incident runbook: rotation is not remediation; drop unknown roles

differences.acceptance: OWNER-ACCEPTED (§2: audit tampering)

differences.acceptance: NEEDS OWNER APPROVAL (not in §2: loss of DBA-01 API/Worker separation)
differences.change: The API process can execute every crewflow_worker-only definer (dispatch claims, release, invite cleanup) and the due-work functions, and terminate the Worker's sessions.

differences.change: Direct SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE on core.worker_due_work across tenants without a definer; dispatch pointers and the deployment marker after SET ROLE.

differences.mitigation: RESET ROLE/DISCARD ALL on checkout + current_user = session_user assertion (mandatory, M0 §6.4 #3)

differences.acceptance: NEEDS OWNER APPROVAL (G-01 reaching an API response on a NORMAL code path; §2 lists cross-organisation authentication data, not invitations)
differences.change: POST member invitations from workspace B for an address workspace A already invited no longer answers 'unavailable': the API discloses another workspace's invitation, because member_invitation is NOT FORCE and the runtime login now sees every tenant's rows. No injection needed.

differences.acceptance: OWNER-ACCEPTED (§2: account takeover) + NEEDS OWNER APPROVAL (column-level grants)
differences.change: user_session: no-context reads return every tenant's sessions; the runtime can write cross-user rows and change absolute_expires_at, user_id and organisation_id (column authority lost).

differences.acceptance: NEEDS OWNER APPROVAL (not in §2: AI execution/skill governance enforced by grants)
differences.change: ai_agent_trigger enable/run_as and standard/system agent edits are no longer refused by grants/policy for the runtime (only the EX-3 CHECK still refuses enabling, 23514); ai_skill name/is_system/organisation_id become updatable. Also measured on deploy e6c768f3: TRUNCATE core.ai_skill is not refused to the runtime login (no TRUNCATE parity guard; TRUNCATE ignores RLS, every tenant) and an INSERT setting organisation_ai_setting.synthetic_data is not refused (no INSERT parity guard). Owner-login CI (PR #74) also measured: the runtime login holds TRUNCATE on ai_usage, ai_conversation, ai_action_proposal and organisation_ai_model_preference through the owner (asserted from the catalog, never executed). UPDATE / DELETE stay row-guarded: ai_action_proposal content is immutable for every role (ai_action_proposal_guard, 23514) and the tenant-column UPDATEs are refused by the parity guards (42501).
differences.keptControl: the EX-3 CHECK constraint still refuses enabled=true without approval for every login (23514)

differences.acceptance: NEEDS OWNER APPROVAL (not in §2: loss of DBA-01-style separation, provisioner-only functions)
differences.change: The ordinary runtime can call the provisioner-only workspace-schema functions (SUPERSEDED fencing's second layer is gone).

differences.acceptance: NEEDS OWNER APPROVAL (not in §2: loss of DBA-01 separation; outbox rows deletable by the runtime)
differences.change: The runtime login can DELETE outbox rows directly on all four outbox tables (retention purge was definer-only).

differences.acceptance: OWNER-ACCEPTED (§2: account takeover and MFA bypass) + NEEDS OWNER APPROVAL (column-level grants)
differences.change: MFA recovery-code hashes and the TOTP secret become readable by the runtime; login_handoff gains table privileges for the runtime.

differences.acceptance: NEEDS OWNER APPROVAL (not in §2: non-secret column-level INSERT grants no longer bind the runtime login)
differences.change: Column INSERT grants that kept server-owned columns out of the runtime's hands (id, created_at, updated_by, expires_at, origin) no longer bind the runtime login, and there is no INSERT parity guard. Measured on the owner-login CI (PR #74): core.ai_usage accepts a forged id / created_at; organisation_ai_model_preference accepts a forged updated_by. RLS WITH CHECK (own organisation, own user) and the INSERT policies still hold: an INSERT for another user / organisation, or a decided proposal (status / decided_by), is still refused.
differences.test: twenty-behaviour-catalogue (owner-login CI: ai-usage-ledger WITH CHECK, ai-model-settings forge, ai-rls T5-D1 INSERT; schema-role checks keep crewflow_app's 42501)

differences.acceptance: NEEDS OWNER APPROVAL (not in §2: global reference tables writable by the runtime login through normal DML)
differences.change: core.permission (RBAC flag reference data) and core.migrations (TypeORM ledger) have no RLS and no organisation_id; the runtime login inherits crewflow's S,I,U,D,T on both (golden :926, :968), so one UPDATE / DELETE changes every tenant. differences.acceptance: OWNER-ACCEPTED (§2: SQL with owner privileges) — table privileges only; no observable effect without context
differences.change: The runtime login holds table privileges on core.host_label_claim / released_host_label / reserved_host_label through the owner (crewflow_app had none). With no tenant context it sees zero rows (FORCE since M-T1, owner-only definer policy) and a DELETE removes nothing; released_host_label stays append-only for every role (trigger); host_label_claim / reserved_host_label writes are parity-guarded.

migratedTests.$comment: Existing suites that assert restricted-runtime-login behaviour. Each must end as: 'catalogue:<id>' (migrated, the difference is above), 'schema-role' (kept: it tests a schema role that still exists, e.g. a definer running as rab_secure_owner), or 'unchanged' (passes as the owner login without asserting a weaker property). Filled from the TW-D differential (run the suite with TEST_DATABASE_URL = crewflow_owner).
migratedTests.status: First pass from the owner-login CI (deploy e6c768f3; worker complete, server complete: PR #74 run 41905033684, 422 suites). Classes: I = identity expectation -> crewflow_owner (BC-02/BC-08); P = schema-role test (superuser SET LOCAL ROLE crewflow_app/crewflow_worker -> 42501) PLUS an owner-side assertion labelled with its catalogue id; M = M-T1 posture effect (reviewed update); L = legacy separate provisioner, skipped by name 'remove in PR #9'. Agent 3 reviews every changed security assertion.
